file: File:Sides of the statue of king Horemheb and queen Mutnedjemet.jpg
description: A double statue of Horemheb and Mutnedjmet was found in Karnak, but is now in the Museo Egizio in Turin (1379). On Mutnedjmet's side of the throne she is depicted as a winged sphinx who adores her own cartouche. As a sphinx she is depicted wearing a flat topped crown topped with plant elements associated with the goddess Tefnut. The back of the statue records Horemheb's rise to power.

file: File:Statue of the god Ptah, granodiorite - Museo Egizio (Turin) C 86 p02.jpg
description: The faces of the statues of gods were patterned after that of the reigning king. Here we recognize the official portrait of Amenhotep III: a rounded, youthful, almost feminine face, with full cheeks, a large smiling mouth, and fleshy lips. The wide and elongated almond-shaped eyes, emphasized by make-up, are particularly characteristic, and so is the relief outline of the lips.
